premarketView.headline: Yields buckle across the curve — 10Y −3bp to 4.75%, 2Y −4bp to 4.33% — and a −0.7 DXY collapse lets QQQ and gold rip together, but the Fed path still prices a 60% September HIKE into a jobs report that lands tomorrow.

sections.body: As of the 16:32:30Z TradingView read (liveNow, ow_macro_rates), the 2Y is 4.332% (−3.9bp on the day) and the 10Y is 4.75% (−3.0bp); the 30Y is 5.234% (−2.6bp) and the 5Y 4.498% (−3.8bp). The 2s10s is +41.8bp (liveNow spread) — a positively-sloped curve that steepens marginally as the front end falls faster than the belly, a bull-steepener in miniature. This is the whole tape's tailwind: yields down across every tenor, and a dollar giving way with them (DXY 98.87, −0.706). Rank the relief by cash-flow duration: longest-duration first. Unprofitable long-duration growth and the most rate-sensitive equity complexes get the largest lift from a −3 to −4bp move — QQQ (716.56, +7.31) leads SPY (772.33, +7.17) precisely because its cash flows sit furthest out. Gold, a zero-coupon perpetual-duration asset, gets the mechanical benefit twice over — falling real yields (DFII10 2.44%, FRED direct asOf 2026-09-01) and a falling dollar — and closes +2.31% at 4489.55 (ow_tv_commodities). At the short, cash-flow-heavy end, financials and value are least helped by the same move; small-caps (IWM +1.02) lag the growth complex despite being rate-sensitive, because their earnings quality, not their duration, is the binding constraint. The one dissonance: the 30Y at 5.234% is still historically elevated — the long end is not confirming any dovish story, it is merely following the front end down a few bp.
sections.title: Rates are the first cause

sections.body: The single most anomalous thing is that the entire risk-and-real-asset complex is rallying — QQQ +7.31, gold +2.31%, silver +2.67% (ow_tv_commodities), VIX 14.58 (−0.61) — while the futures-implied Fed path still carries a 60% probability of a 25bp HIKE at the 9/16 meeting (Frenzy Capital fed-funds futures via argon, snapshot 2026-09-02; futures-implied, NOT CME FedWatch). Equities and metals are trading a rate-cut regime; the policy strip is pricing a rate-HIKE regime. The reconciling variable is the dollar and the front end: the market is leaning on a soft labour read tomorrow to break the tie, and the expectations bar it faces is unusually low — the payrolls consensus is +50k against a prior print of −23k (ow_uw_calendar). That is the bar that makes today's move legible: risk is not pricing strength, it is pricing a labour market weak enough (prior −23k) to override the hike path, and the dollar collapse (−0.706 DXY) is the tell that the crowd is positioned for the dovish resolution. It is a bet placed the day before the number, not a reaction to one — which is why VIX easing to 14.58 into a payrolls print is itself part of the anomaly.
sections.title: Today's largest divergence

sections.body: No beat-and-raise names can be tagged today: the ow_uw_headlines feed (25 rows, newest 2026-09-03T16:21:01Z) carries no corporate earnings beat-and-raise print that closed down — the tape is early-September, between earnings seasons, and the day's headlines are macro, geopolitical and product-news, not guidance revisions. Note the tape is intraday-live, not a closing read (current instant 12:32 ET), so no name has a settled 'closed down' mark yet. Named for the record, verbatim as citation: 2026-09-03T16:01:05Z — 'US MORTGAGE RATES CLIMB TO 6.71%, HIGHEST SINCE JULY 2025' — a rate-tightening signal at the household level that sits oddly against the bond rally. With no beat-and-raise-but-down name available, this section has no tag today.
sections.title: Good news, priced down = pricing power exhausted

sections.body: WHEN/WHO from ow_uw_calendar: Hammack (Cleveland) and Goolsbee (Chicago) speak at 2026-09-03T19:00:00Z (3:00 PM ET) at a 'Connecting Communities' event; the payrolls complex lands 2026-09-04T12:30:00Z (8:30 AM ET). The reaction function, read off the rates liveNow and not guessed: the strip prices a 60% HIKE for 9/16 and a 64% HIKE by 12/9 (Frenzy Capital via argon, snapshot 2026-09-02, futures-implied, not CME FedWatch), yet the 2Y fell 3.9bp today — so the front end is fading the hike odds ahead of the data, not confirming them. The conditioning variable is spelled out in a citation, verbatim: 2026-09-03T15:31:58Z (ow_uw_headlines) — 'Fed Governor Christopher Waller now leans toward a conditional September hold, according to WSJ's Nick Timiraos. If August inflation keeps moving toward 2%, he favors no change; a hot print could put a rate hike back in play.' That is a reaction function stated in the conditional: hold if disinflation continues, hike if inflation runs hot. I do not predict which branch fires. The read for the tape is only that a −4bp 2Y move plus a −0.7 DXY move is the market pre-committing to the dovish branch before Hammack/Goolsbee speak and before tomorrow's number sets the condition.
sections.title: Reaction function (policy speech stripped)

sections.body: Transmission order: the number hits the front end first. A payrolls read at or below +35k — especially with the unemployment rate ticking to 4.2% and AHE at or below 0.2% m/m — lets the 2Y (liveNow 4.33%, −4.1bp today) break lower through the 4.30% shelf; the strip's 60% September hike odds (Frenzy Capital via argon, snapshot 2026-09-02, futures-implied not CME FedWatch) collapse toward a hold or a cut discussion. Second, the dollar extends its give (DXY liveNow 98.871, already −0.705 today) because rate differentials compress. Third — and only third — equities and real assets take the baton: QQQ (716.56) leads SPY (772.33) because its cash flows sit furthest out and gain most from a lower discount rate, and gold (4489.55) gets the double lift of a lower real yield (DFII10 2.44%, FRED asOf 2026-09-01) and a softer dollar. The 30Y (5.234%) is the laggard and the tell — it follows the front down only a few bp, so 2s10s steepens past +42bp. The today-tape's pre-positioning (net call premium built to +$394mm intraday before fading to +$133mm by 16:33Z) is the crowd already leaning this way.
sections.title: Path A — Cool print, dovish resolution (prior confirmed weak, ≤35k with steady/higher UR)

sections.body: Transmission order: nothing moves decisively first because the number resolves nothing. A headline in the 35k–65k band around the +50k consensus with a 4.1% UR keeps the hike-vs-hold argument exactly where it stood — the 2Y round-trips a few bp intraday and settles near 4.33–4.36%, the 30Y barely twitches. Second, with rates inert, the dollar holds its post-selloff level near 98.9 and gives equities no fresh fuel. Third, the tape mean-reverts: today's +7-handle gains in SPY/QQQ are given partial back as the pre-data long that was placed yesterday gets monetized into an event that failed to confirm it. VIX (liveNow 14.57), already compressed into the print, has no reason to fall further and drifts back toward its 1-Sep 16.34 close as hedges are re-struck ahead of the 9/16 FOMC. This is the 'buy-the-rumor, no news' path where the anomaly the regime flagged — risk pricing cuts while the strip prices a hike — simply persists unresolved.
sections.title: Path B — In-line print, tie unbroken (35k–65k, UR 4.1%, AHE 0.2%)

sections.body: Transmission order: the front end reprices first and violently. A payrolls beat above +90k, or AHE at 0.4%+ m/m regardless of the headline, validates the Waller conditional's hawkish branch ('a hot print could put a rate hike back in play,' WSJ/Timiraos via ow_uw_headlines 2026-09-03T15:31:58Z). The 2Y jumps back through 4.40%+ toward 4.45%, hike odds firm from 60% toward 75%+. Second, the dollar snaps back — DXY reclaims 99.5+ as differentials widen — which is the mechanical hit to metals: gold and silver, the pure-duration real assets that led today, reverse hardest first. Third, equities absorb the damage in reverse duration order: QQQ (the longest-duration leader) sells off more than SPY, and the today-gain in both is erased. IWM (295.03), rate-sensitive but earnings-quality-constrained, underperforms on a double hit of higher discount rate and no growth relief. 2s10s flattens as the front end leads the whole curve up.
sections.title: Path C — Hot print, hike back on (≥90k or AHE ≥0.4% m/m)

sections.body: Transmission order: this is the path where good-for-rates becomes bad-for-risk. A print worse than −50k with the UR spiking to 4.4%+ sends the 2Y sharply lower first (through 4.25%) as cuts get pulled forward — but the signal transmits second into credit, not equity relief: HY OAS (2.66%, FRED asOf 2026-09-02, ~2-day lag; daily mirror BAMLH0A0HYM2 at 2.65 on 2026-09-01) widens as the market reprices recession odds rather than a soft landing. Third, equities break the correlation they held all of today: QQQ and SPY sell off *with* falling yields because the discount-rate relief is swamped by an earnings-recession fear, and VIX (14.57) spikes back above 17. Gold is the one asset that still works here — it gets the falling-real-yield lift without the credit penalty. The curve bull-steepens aggressively but for the wrong reason: it is a growth-scare steepener, the mirror image of Path A's relief steepener.
sections.title: Path D — Ugly print, growth scare overrides the cut trade (deeply negative, <−50k, UR jumps to 4.4%+)

sections.body: Base case: Path A (cool print, dovish resolution), assigned modestly above even odds against B as the main alternative. The reason is the setup, not a forecast of the number: the consensus bar is set at +50k against a prior of −23k, an unusually low hurdle that makes a sub-consensus print the path of least resistance, and the entire tape has already pre-committed to that resolution — the 2Y fell 4.1bp and DXY fell 0.705 *ahead of* the data, while today's option flow built net call premium to +$394mm before fading. When the front end and the dollar move dovishly the day before a number, and the number's bar is a −23k prior, the base case is that the data ratifies the lean rather than fighting it. I choose A over B (the unresolved tie) because a flat in-line print still leaves the strip's 60% hike odds standing into 9/16, and the market's revealed positioning says it is unwilling to sit in that limbo — it wants the low bar cleared downward. What tips A over D: the 30Y at 5.234% is not confirming any recession story, and HY OAS at 2.66% is near the low end of its 30-day range (2.60–2.75), so credit is pricing soft landing, not stress.
sections.title: Base case and the reason

sections.body: Payrolls (2026-09-04T12:30:00Z / 8:30 AM ET), the tie-breaker. Path A CONFIRMS on the combination {headline ≤35k AND (UR ≥4.1% OR AHE ≤0.2% m/m) AND 2Y trades below 4.30% AND DXY holds below 98.9}; it is FALSIFIED if headline prints ≥65k OR the 2Y closes back above 4.38% OR DXY reclaims 99.5 — any one of those breaks the dovish transmission chain even on a soft headline. Path C CONFIRMS on {headline ≥90k OR AHE ≥0.4% m/m} together with {2Y above 4.40% AND DXY above 99.5}; it is FALSIFIED if a hot headline is met by a *falling* 2Y (which would mean the market disbelieves the strength). Path D CONFIRMS on {headline <−50k AND UR ≥4.4% AND HY OAS widening AND QQQ falling while 2Y falls}; it is FALSIFIED the moment equities *rally* on the weak print (that is Path A, not D) or HY OAS fails to widen. Path B is the residual: CONFIRMED by {headline 35k–65k AND UR 4.1% AND 2Y within ±3bp of 4.33% two hours post-print}, FALSIFIED by any decisive break of the front end in either direction. The Hammack/Goolsbee remarks earlier (2026-09-03T19:00:00Z / 3:00 PM ET) are a lower-tier catalyst: they CONFIRM the dovish lean only if the 2Y extends lower into the speeches, and are FALSIFIED as a mover if the front end ignores them — a speech that moves nothing is the base expectation the day before payrolls.
sections.title: Confirmation vs falsification per catalyst

sections.body: The dominant reverse risk is not that the number comes in hot — it is that the number comes in soft and equities *still* fall, collapsing Path A into Path D. The whole tape today is built on a single load-bearing correlation: falling yields lifting risk. That correlation is a soft-landing assumption, and it is fragile precisely because a −23k prior is already a contracting-payrolls signal. If tomorrow's print confirms deterioration rather than mere cooling — a deeply negative headline with a rising unemployment rate — the market can flip in an instant from pricing the discount-rate relief (bullish QQQ) to pricing the earnings recession (bearish everything but gold), and the pre-positioned longs shown in today's flow (net call premium peaking at +$394mm) become forced sellers into a bid that has vanished. VIX at 14.57, compressed into the event, is not protection — it is fuel, because there is no hedge cushion to unwind gently. A second, quieter reverse risk sits on the long end: the 30Y at 5.234% has refused to confirm the dovish story all day. If a soft payrolls print sends the front end down but the 30Y *rises* on fiscal/supply concerns, the resulting bear-steepener would undercut the duration-relief trade that QQQ and gold are leaning on, and the equity rally could stall even on a 'good' number for the front end. Either way, the reverse case does not need a hawkish surprise — it only needs the risk-and-rates correlation to break, and that break is more likely on a bad number than a good one.

intradayHeadline: Curve bull-steepens as 2Y sheds 3.5bp into Friday's payroll, gold rips to $4,486 — and Broadcom's soft Q4 guide sinks it 3% against a green SMH tape, the tell that the AI-capex bar has outrun even the winners.

intradayRegimeSections.body: The 2Y sits at 4.336% (−3.5bp) and the 10Y at 4.752% (−2.8bp) on TradingView's live curve (ow_macro_rates liveNow, fetchedAt 2026-09-03T17:00:20.911Z). The front end is leading the rally, so the 2s10s steepens to +41.6bp — a bull-steepener the day before payrolls, the front end pulling down harder than the belly. Note the shape is inverted-turned-positive at the long end: the 30Y at 5.234% (−2.6bp) sits well above the 10Y. This is the 'good' direction for duration — everything is richer — but the level still bites. Rank by cash-flow duration, from most-helped-to-most-exposed: the longest-duration equity — unprofitable-until-2030 growth, the crypto-treasury and small-cap complex (IWM +0.98 to 294.99) — gets the biggest present-value tailwind from lower discount rates and is why the front-end rally matters; long-bond proxies (TLT 82.325, +0.375) get a direct mark-up; mega-cap tech (QQQ +8.38) rides it comfortably. The hurt is muted today because rates fell across the whole curve — but the 30Y above 5.2% is the reminder that the term-premium floor under long-duration cash flows has not moved.
intradayRegimeSections.title: Rates are the first cause

intradayRegimeSections.body: Broadcom. AVGO trades 356.37, down −10.87 (~−3%), while the entire semi and mega-cap tape it anchors is green: SMH's sector complex bid, NVDA +3.07 to 227.48, MRVL +5.27 to 211.75, ALAB +5.60 to 279.73, XLK +2.25 to 185.845, QQQ +8.38. A name falling 3% inside a rallying group it is a bellwether of is the anomaly. The cause is the expectations bar, not sentiment: Broadcom did not miss on the print, it guided the top line light. Per Unusual Whales, 2026-09-02T20:17:34Z — 'BROADCOM SEES 4Q REV. ABOUT $34.8B, EST. $35.05B' — and 2026-09-02T20:20:20Z — 'BROADCOM TUMBLES 6.8% AFTER 4Q REVENUE OUTLOOK MISSES ESTIMATE.' The bar for the AI-infrastructure leaders is now set at beat-AND-raise; a merely-in-line-to-soft revenue outlook, against a stock that had front-run tens of billions of AI chip financing, is enough to sink it while its peers rally on the same AI-capex thesis. The sell-side confirms the re-rate: Unusual Whales, 2026-09-03T13:40:29Z — 'BofA Global Research cuts Broadcom's price objective to $460 from $530.' The divergence is the market marking down the marginal dollar of AI revenue at the one name where the expectations bar had climbed highest.
intradayRegimeSections.title: Today's largest divergence

intradayRegimeSections.body: No clean beat-and-raise-that-closed-down name surfaces in today's coverage. The one large decliner into a green tape, Broadcom, is a guide-DOWN (Q4 revenue outlook of ~$34.8B below the ~$35.05B estimate, per Unusual Whales 2026-09-02T20:17:34Z), not a beat-and-raise — so it does not carry this tag; it is treated as the divergence above. Absent a beat-and-raise print marked down today, the pricing-power-exhausted signal does not fire. Flagging the absence rather than forcing a name onto the tag: the tell to watch tomorrow is whether an in-line-or-better payroll fails to lift the long-duration complex.
intradayRegimeSections.title: Good news, priced down = pricing power exhausted

intradayRegimeSections.body: Two Fed voices are dated for today — Cleveland's Hammack and Chicago's Goolsbee, 'Connecting Communities' remarks at 2026-09-03T19:00:00Z (ow_uw_calendar, asOf 2026-09-03T17:00:23.127Z) — but the reaction is read off the tape, not guessed forward. What the front end is already pricing: the futures-implied path (ow_argon_policy_path, Frenzy Capital fed-funds futures via argon, snapshot 2026-09-02 — futures-implied via Frenzy Capital, NOT CME FedWatch) has the 9/16 meeting at a 60% HIKE / 40% Hold, implied rate 3.78%, target 3.75–4.00%; then 10/28 leaning HOLD at 70%; then 12/9 back to a 64% HIKE. That is a market pricing a Fed still in a tightening-bias reaction function — the input that matters is inflation/labor running hot enough to justify hikes, not cuts. Yet today the 2Y richened 3.5bp and the curve bull-steepened, and gold ripped +2.23% to $4,486 with silver +2.53% and DXY −0.71 to 98.864 (ow_tv_commodities, asOf 2026-09-03T17:00:26.278Z; ow_macro_rates liveNow) — a real-asset, weaker-dollar bid that reads as the market fading the hike-path stiffness ahead of tomorrow's 08:30 ET payroll (consensus +50k jobs, prior −23k; unemployment 4.1% vs 4.1% prior; AHE +0.2% m/m). The reaction function in one line: the front end says a soft labor print pulls the September hike odds down fast, and the gold/dollar move is the early vote for that.
